Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Karan Singh Dugtal, learned counsel
for the applicant.
2. Ms. Pushpa Bhatt, learned Addl.
Advocate General along with Mr. S.C. Dumka,
learned A.G.A. and Mr. Nikhil Bisht, learned
Brief Holder for the State.
3. Applicant- Simran Sahni, who is in
judicial custody in connection with FIR/Case
Crime No. 00637 of 2026 under Sections
8/20 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic
Substances Act, 1985, registered at Police
Station Patelnagar, District Dehradun, has
sought her release on bail.
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties
and perused the material available on record.
5. As per the prosecution case, during
routine checking, the police party allegedly
apprehended the applicant and, upon
searching the carrying bag found in her
possession, recovered 3.012 grams of the
alleged contraband, stated to be ganja, along
with ₹600/-. On the basis of the said
recovery, the F.I.R. came to be registered

against the applicant for the alleged offence
under the provisions of the N.D.P.S. Act.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant would
further submit that the alleged contraband is
stated to contain green leaves, which, in the
absence of the flowering or fruiting tops of the
cannabis plant, do not fall within the
definition of ganja under Section 2(iii)(b) of
the N.D.P.S. Act. He would further submit
that the alleged quantity of contraband
recovered from the applicant is less than the
commercial quantity and, therefore, the
rigours of Section 37 of the N.D.P.S. Act are
not attracted, subject to the nature and
classification of the alleged substance.
7. Learned counsel would further submit
that the mandatory provisions of the N.D.P.S.
Act have not been duly complied with during
the search and seizure proceedings. He would
contend that the personal search of the
applicant was conducted by a woman police
constable and not before a Gazetted Officer,
thereby raising a question regarding
compliance with the applicable statutory
safeguards. He would further submit that the
applicant has been languishing in judicial
custody since 14.09.2026; that she is a
permanent resident of District Dehradun and,
therefore, there is no likelihood of her
absconding; and that the trial is not likely to
conclude in the near future. On these
grounds, learned counsel submits that the
applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
8. Per contra, learned State counsel would
vehemently oppose the prayer for bail,
however, he does not dispute that the
applicant is in judicial custody since

14.09.2026
9. Having considered the submissions
advanced by learned counsel for the parties,
the nature of the allegations, the
circumstances surrounding the alleged
recovery, the contentions regarding conscious
possession, and the period of incarceration
undergone by the applicant, this Court is of
the view that the applicant has made out a
case for bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any
opinion on the merits of the case, the bail
application is allowed on the following
conditions:-
(a) The applicant shall execute a personal
bond and furnish two reliable sureties in
the like amount to the satisfaction of the
trial court.
(b) The applicant shall not leave the
country without prior permission of the
court.
(c) The applicant shall appear before the
investigating officer as and when required
and cooperate with the investigation.
(d) The applicant shall not tamper with
evidence or witnesses, either directly or
indirectly and shall not indulge in any
criminal activity while on bail.
(e) The applicant shall surrender their
passport, if any, to the court or to the
investigating agency, to preclude risk of
absconding.
11. The bail granted to the applicant shall be
liable to be cancelled in the event of any
violation of the aforesaid conditions or if the
applicant is found to have misused the liberty
granted to them.
 (Alok Mahra, J.)
